steps.title: Mount the motor and capture the case nuts
steps.action: Load six M3 nuts from below the plate. Seat the plate on the motor pilot and install four M3 x 8 countersunk screws with heads 0.5 mm proud of its top face.

steps.title: Fit the cage with its captive nuts
steps.action: Seat twelve M2 nuts underneath the lower cage, then lower the cage teeth upward onto the plate.

steps.title: Prepare and fit the lower eccentric
steps.action: Load two M3 joint nuts from below. Slide the lower eccentric onto the motor shaft with its bearing journal upward. Locate the small semicircular mark on the edge of the lower collar.

steps.title: Fit the lower wave half and 6704
steps.action: Seat four M3 nuts underneath the lower clamshell. Lower it around the eccentric journal and seat the 6704 bearing squarely in its recess.

steps.title: Close the eccentric shaft
steps.action: Load the radial M3 nut from the top of the upper eccentric and start its M3 x 8 clamp screw. Align the semicircular edge marks at the middle of the bearing. Tighten the two M3 x 20 countersunk joiners, then tighten the upper shaft clamp before fitting the outer case.

steps.title: Close the wave clamshell
steps.action: Fit the upper wave half around the 6704 bearing. Tighten four M3 x 12 countersunk screws into the lower nuts.

steps.title: Lower the fixed ring
steps.action: Confirm the upper shaft clamp is tight, then lower the fixed ring around the cage and align all six fins with the base.

steps.title: Insert twelve rollers
steps.action: At input angle zero, insert one 7 mm OD x 12 mm nylon spacer in each cage slot.

steps.title: Fit and fasten the upper cage
steps.action: Load four M3 output nuts underneath the upper cage, then lower it over the teeth. Install all twelve M2 x 20 countersunk screws through the disc into the lower cage nuts.

steps.title: Fit the output bearing and close the case
steps.action: Seat the 6810 over the upper cage hub. Lower the housing over the bearing outer race. Insert six M3 x 35 socket caps from the top and tighten into the captive base nuts.

steps.title: Preassemble the output plate
steps.action: Load 4 M6 and 4 M3 attachment nuts into the carrier and two M3 sandwich nuts from underneath. Fit the flat cover and tighten two M3 x 10 countersunk screws. The plate is now clamped as a separate assembly; its viewing hole and bolt-clearance holes stay open.

steps.title: Close the output face
steps.action: Lower the preassembled output plate over the bearing and fasten it to the cage with four M3 x 20 countersunk screws. Keep the separate short sandwich screws tight. With power disconnected, hand-turn the input 12 times for one reverse output turn and observe the shaft through the 20 mm opening.

book.project_summary: A 3D-printable 12:1 roller wave gearbox for a NEMA 17 motor, with an OOBB mounting base and output face. Twelve nylon spacers transfer motion from an eccentric wheel to the output cage. The output turns once in the opposite direction for every 12 motor turns.
details: Reduction: 12:1. Output rotates opposite to the motor.
Motor: NEMA 17, 40 mm body, 24 mm shaft.
Rollers: 12 nylon spacers, 7 mm OD, 12 mm depth, 3.2 mm bore.
Cage: M2 x 20 countersunk screws; 1.6 mm nominal tip clearance.
Eccentric joint: M3 x 20 countersunk screws and captive nuts.
Clamshell joint: M3 x 12 countersunk screws and captive nuts.
Case: M3 x 35 screws from above; nuts underneath the base.
Motor mount: M3 x 8 countersunk screws.
Output: 20 mm viewing hole; 4 M6 and 4 M3 attachment nuts.
Output sandwich: two M3 x 10 short joiners, separate from the cage fixings.
Tighten the upper shaft clamp before fitting the outer case.
Optional lifter on standard upper collar: two M3 x 35 socket-cap joiners.
